Patient: I'm 61 years old, male, and I'm here because I've been having back pain that's been getting worse over the last few days. Doctor: Can you describe the location of your back pain, whether it radiates to other areas, its severity on a scale of 1 to 10, how long it has been present, and what makes it better or worse? Patient: The pain started on the right side of my back, but it's been shifting and now it's more on the left. It's been going on for about four days. Tylenol doesn't seem to help much. Additionally, have you had any recent urinary tract infections, kidney stones, or other urological issues? Patient: The blood in my urine is kind of hard to detect, but it does look a little off-color. I haven't noticed any burning or urgency, just that it looks different. I had kidney stones about two years ago, but nothing recently. Patient: I don't have any numbness or weakness, but I do feel some body aches because I'm favoring my back when I walk.
